justifications.c1: EoW is costly in aggregate (ABI £2m-£2.7m/day via CILA, Insurance Times search-confirmed, Zurich) and Confused.com gives £5,708 per incident vs Which? £1,200; no probate/unoccupied-home claim value or incidence, so per-estate expected loss is unknown.
justifications.c2: Insurer condition requires an inspection at least every 14 days with a dated record (Homeprotect, search-confirmed) for the whole unoccupied period, plus winter drain-down/heating conditions (UK Insurance Net); fortnightly, not weekly.
justifications.c3: Paid workarounds with prices: Carter Jonas key holding + monthly inspections from £300/month, void inspector paid £15 per 45-60 min visit (DWP), Safesite monitored alarm £35/week; whether a sensor would let insurers relax in-person visits is unproven.
justifications.c4: Insurer wording requires dated inspection records and drain-down/heating in winter (Homeprotect, brokers) and FOS decisions (DRN-3771411, DRN-5887323) show EoW claims on unoccupied/estate homes being declined and disputed; one Homeprotect exclusion page unconfirmed.
justifications.c5: Executors are mostly one-off lay individuals or solicitors paid from the estate; no job advert or budget evidence (researcher found none); payer is fragmented and consumer-like.
justifications.c6: Specialist probate insurers/brokers set the conditions (Homeprotect, UK Insurance Net), Eddisons RemoteZone and property-visit networks (Viewber) serve vacant homes, and Hiscox already bundles LeakBot free for buildings policyholders (adjacent niche).
justifications.c7: Willingness to pay shown by Safesite (£35/week), Carter Jonas (£300/month) and insurer-backed LeakBot; researcher found no product rented per estate that outputs inspection/drain-down evidence for the probate insurer.
justifications.c8: Commodity leak sensors and shut-off valves exist (Grohe) and battery cellular vacant-property kits are deployed (Safesite); no BOM, and a flow sensor on the incoming main may need a plumber (inference).
justifications.c9: Records are required on the insurer's 14-day schedule and comparable hire runs ~£35/week, but revenue per estate ends at sale (built-in churn) and no per-estate rental duration is sourced.
justifications.c10: Ombudsman decisions (FOS), ABI loss data via trade press (Insurance Times, CILA), probate trade press (Today's Wills and Probate) and a Parliamentary committee linking probate to empty homes.

weakest: There is no sourced figure for how often probate homes suffer escape-of-water losses or what they cost, and the payer is a one-off lay executor rather than a budget-holding professional.
